newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums stagnate as screen slumps.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums stagnate as screen slumps.

text.p: NWE gas oil physical markets stagnated on Wednesday on flat prompt demand and further caution inspired by a plunge in screen values, traders said.
"It's very thin, very quiet. The market is preparing for demand coming up next month rather than prompt business," one trader said.

Benchmark Dec and Jan IPE futures slumped $10.25 and $9.75 to $203 and $204.75 a tonne respectively after bearish API stock data and confirmation that Iraqi crude had started flowing in earnest to Turkey.
An arbitrage to Asia was seen workable from the Med but the fall in the screen complicated efforts to pursue further an arb from NWE seen earlier in the week, the traders said.
Refinery grade heating oil was notionally around Jan IPE +$5.25/6, with Russians around Jan IPE -$1. Low sulphur diesel was put at Jan IPE +$14/16.
On barges, refinery heating oil was done in scattered trades at Dec IPE -$1/+0.50. Low sulphur diesel was around Dec IPE +$10/11, around unchanged.
Traders said they did not expect a large physical delivery on the Dec IPE expiry on Thursday.
